In Python, what is a variable?¶{{c1::A name stuck on a value ("a labelled jar") — reassigning moves the label, not the contents}}
What are Python's three starter types and their literals?¶Text {{c1::str "text"}} · whole number {{c1::int 42}} · decimal {{c1::float 12.5}}
In Python, what does "2" + "2" evaluate to?¶{{c1::"22" — + on strings glues text; convert with int() first if you meant maths}}
In Python, what is the difference between return and print?¶return {{c1::hands a value to the caller — usable, storable, testable}}; print {{c1::only shows pixels to a human}}
What is a parameter vs an argument?¶Parameter = {{c1::the placeholder name in the def}}; argument = {{c1::the actual value passed in the call}}
In Python, what type does input() always return?¶{{c1::str — even if the user typed a number; convert before arithmetic}}
In Python, what is = vs ==?¶= {{c1::assigns (sticks the label)}}; == {{c1::compares (asks a True/False question)}}
Which branch of a Python if/elif chain runs?¶{{c1::The FIRST true one only, the rest are skipped — so the narrowest/highest test goes first}}
In Python, what owns an indented block?¶{{c1::The if/for/while/def line above it — indentation IS the syntax; four spaces}}
In Python, when do you use for vs while?¶for = {{c1::for each thing in a collection}}; while = {{c1::keep going until this stops being true}}
What are the four steps of the accumulator pattern?¶{{c1::Start the accumulator}} · {{c1::visit each item}} · {{c1::fold it in}} · {{c1::return the result}}
What is the first index of a Python list, and what does items[len(items)] raise?¶{{c1::0}} · {{c1::IndexError — the last valid index is len(items)-1}}
How do you read a Python traceback?¶{{c1::Bottom-up — the last line is what went wrong, the lines above are where}}
Why never write a bare except: in Python?¶{{c1::It swallows EVERY alarm, including the typo you needed to hear — catch the specific exception}}
What is the Python retry-until-valid input idiom?¶{{c1::while True + try/break on success + except ValueError: ask again}}
In Python, what is sys.argv[0]?¶{{c1::The script's own name — the first real argument is sys.argv[1]}}
What is the fastest Python laboratory you own?¶{{c1::The REPL — run python alone, experiment one line at a time, exit()}}
What three things make a unit test GOOD?¶{{c1::It fails when behaviour breaks}} · {{c1::it tests boundaries (0/empty/negative)}} · {{c1::its name says what it guards}}
Why can't you assert on print in a test?¶{{c1::print returns None — structure logic in functions that RETURN, then assert on the value}}
What is the safe file-reading idiom in Python?¶{{c1::with open(path) as f: — closes the file for you, even when errors happen}}
In Python's open(), what do modes "w" and "a" do?¶"w" {{c1::REPLACES the file's contents}}; "a" {{c1::appends}}
What is the phantom \n bug when reading files?¶{{c1::Lines keep their newline — .strip() (or .rstrip("\n")) before comparing}}
What is the count-dict idiom using a plain dict and .get (no imports)?¶{{c1::counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1}}
In regex, what match a digit, a word-char, one-or-more, optional, one-of-these, a capture group?¶{{c1::\d}} · {{c1::\w}} · {{c1::+}} · {{c1::?}} · {{c1::[abc]}} · {{c1::()}}
Why use raw strings for Python regex?¶{{c1::r"..." stops Python eating backslashes before the regex engine sees them}}
What regex matches every dd/mm/yyyy date?¶{{c1::r"\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}" — with re.findall to pull them all}}
In OOP, what is a class vs an object?¶Class = {{c1::the cookie cutter (blueprint)}}; object = {{c1::the cookie (instance) — "hi".upper() is a method on a str object}}
In Python, what is self?¶{{c1::The object being operated on — passed to methods automatically}}
In Python, what does @property do?¶{{c1::Makes a method readable like an attribute — w.volume, no parentheses}}
In Python, what does __str__ control?¶{{c1::What print(obj) and str(obj) show — the human face of your object}}
Write a Python list comprehension for the squares of the even numbers in nums:¶{{c1::[x*x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]}}
In Python, sort a dict's items by value descending, ties alphabetical:¶{{c1::sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))}}
De-duplicate a Python list in one call — order-free, then deduped AND sorted:¶{{c1::set(items)}} · {{c1::sorted(set(items))}}
